elements.id-string-11: In this paper, via a covariant semitetrad spacetime decomposition, we present a novel geometrical classification of shear-free Locally Rotationally Symmetric (LRS-II) perfect fluid self-gravitating systems, in terms of the covariantly defined fluid acceleration and the fluid expansion.
elements.id-string-12: We further analyze the interesting class of these systems that are dynamic, necessarily inhomogeneous with tidal deformations and yet shear-free.
elements.id-string-13: We deduce the governing highly non-linear differential equation that gives the possible equations of state of matter that can lead to such a scenario.
elements.id-string-14: We find that the possible equations of state are very limited.{\bf Keywords: } spacetime decomposition, shear-free fluids, equation of state
elements.id-string-16: Spherical shear-free self-gravitating systems of perfect fluids are perhaps the most well studied systems in the historical quest for exact solutions of the Einstein field equations, and as rightly pointed out by \cite{exact}, is rich in rediscoveries.
elements.id-string-17: All the known solutions are presented in \cite{McVittie, Kustaan, Wyman}, while in all later works these solutions are always contained as special cases.
elements.id-string-18: Generally, there are three different approaches to find exact solutions of the field equations for shear-free and spherical perfect fluid distributions.
elements.id-string-19: The first approach is via an adhoc ansatz for one of the metric functions, while the second one is to look for symmetries including Lie point symmetries, contact symmetries and Noether symmetries in the field equations.
elements.id-string-20: The third approach is more general and rigorous, where the solutions have Painlev\'{e} properties \cite{Wyman}.
elements.id-string-21: As a matter of fact, all the known solutions belong to this latter class.
elements.id-string-22: In this paper, we investigate this well studied system through a more geometrical perspective.
elements.id-string-23: In fact, we generalize the spacetime geometry to Locally Rotationally Symmetric (LRS-II) spacetimes \cite{vanElstEllis}, of which spherical symmetry is a subclass.
elements.id-string-24: By covariantly decomposing the spacetime using the fluid flow congruence and a preferred spherical congruence which is guaranteed by LRS-II symmetry, we classify all the possible solutions of the field equations in terms of the covariantly defined fluid acceleration and the fluid expansion.
elements.id-string-25: Interestingly, our analysis sheds new light on the class of solutions where fluid acceleration and expansion are strictly non-vanishing.
elements.id-string-26: It can easily be seen that the Weyl curvature is also non-vanishing for this class.
elements.id-string-27: This class is interesting as it is dynamical and necessarily inhomogeneous but still shear-free.
elements.id-string-28: It is well known that spacetime shear and the electric part of the Weyl form a feedback loop with each other.
elements.id-string-29: The electric part of the Weyl is a source term for the shear evolution equation while the shear is the source term for the evolution of the electric part of the Weyl.
elements.id-string-30: Therefore, constraining one of these quantities to vanish identically, while the other is strictly non-vanishing, would imply a stringent constraint on other geometrical and thermodynamical quantities in the spacetime.
elements.id-string-31: From our analysis, we transparently show that indeed such a stringent constraint exists on the possible equations of state that give rise to this class.
elements.id-string-32: We find the governing ODE, which is highly non-linear, the solution to which gives the possible classes of equations of state that may give rise to this class of solutions.
elements.id-string-33: We present a numerical solution for this ODE and clearly show that the usual equations of state that are linear, or a finite combination of power law solutions, will not generate the given class.
elements.id-string-34: The paper is organized as follows: In the next two sections we discuss the covariant semitetrad decomposition of the spacetime manifold, and the field equations written in terms of geometrical and thermodynamical variables that emerge due to the decomposition.
elements.id-string-35: In the subsequent two sections we discuss the special case of shear-free spacetimes, and show how all possible solutions can be classified in terms of the fluid acceleration and the fluid expansion.
elements.id-string-36: The next section is dedicated to the interesting class of inhomogeneous and shear-free spacetimes, and the differential equation that governs the equation of state of the perfect fluid.
elements.id-string-37: Finally, we conclude our results in the last section.
